data.name: Reason_KernelOrSystemProcess_Explain
data.value: Part of the Windows kernel. SnapBack never touches it.

data.name: Reason_OtherSession_Explain
data.value: Runs in a different Windows session (system services or another signed-in user).

data.name: Reason_OtherUser_Explain
data.value: Runs under a different user account.

data.name: Reason_CriticalProcess_Explain
data.value: Windows marks this process as critical: ending it would crash the computer.

data.name: Reason_ProtectedProcess_Explain
data.value: Windows protects this process (for example anti-malware or DRM).

data.name: Reason_ServiceHost_Explain
data.value: Hosts a Windows service. SnapBack does not manage services.

data.name: Reason_ShellComponent_Explain
data.value: An essential part of the Windows desktop, session or security.

data.name: Reason_Elevated_Explain
data.value: Runs with administrator rights. SnapBack never touches elevated programs.

data.name: Reason_AccessDenied_Explain
data.value: Windows does not allow SnapBack to inspect this process.

data.name: Reason_OwnerUnknown_Explain
data.value: The owner of this process could not be verified.

data.name: Reason_ImagePathUnknown_Explain
data.value: The executable of this process could not be verified.

data.name: Reason_CannotVerify_Explain
data.value: Some safety attributes of this process could not be verified.

data.name: Reason_ConsoleProgram_Explain
data.value: May be running a job; stopping it can interrupt work in progress.

data.name: Reason_ScriptOrRuntime_Explain
data.value: Python, Node.js and similar runtimes may be in the middle of a task.

data.name: Reason_NoWindow_Explain
data.value: Has no window, so it cannot be asked to close politely.

data.name: Reason_VirtualMachine_Explain
data.value: Closing it may stop a virtual machine and lose its unsaved state.

data.name: Reason_InstallerOrUpdater_Explain
data.value: Interrupting it may leave an installation broken.

data.name: Reason_LaunchedSnapBack_Explain
data.value: SnapBack was launched from this program; closing it may close SnapBack too.

data.name: Reason_WindowsUserTool_Explain
data.value: A tool that ships with Windows.

data.name: Reason_PossibleUnsavedWork_Explain
data.value: Editors, IDEs and office apps may hold unsaved documents. They are asked to close normally, so they can prompt you.

data.name: Reason_UnsavedChangesInTitle_Explain
data.value: A window title indicates unsaved changes.

data.name: Reason_Browser_Explain
data.value: Tabs are usually restored, but downloads in progress and unsent forms may be lost.

data.name: Reason_Terminal_Explain
data.value: Closing a terminal ends every shell and command running in it.

data.name: Reason_SyncOrTransfer_Explain
data.value: Sync, torrent and download apps may be in the middle of a transfer.

data.name: Reason_Launcher_Explain
data.value: Game and app launchers may be downloading or installing updates.

data.name: Reason_Recording_Explain
data.value: May be recording or streaming right now.

data.name: Reason_NotResponding_Explain
data.value: The app is not responding at the moment.

data.name: Reason_NewInstanceOfBaselineApp_Explain
data.value: Another instance of this app was already running at the baseline.

data.name: Reason_StartedByBaselineApp_Explain
data.value: Started by an app that was already running at the baseline; it may still need it.

data.name: Reason_RunsInBackground_Explain
data.value: No visible window (for example minimized to the tray).

data.value: Ask {0} (PID {1}) to exit through Windows Restart Manager, the way installers do (never forced).

data.value: {0} (PID {1}) has no window to close politely; it will only be reported as still running.

data.value: If the app asks to save changes, SnapBack waits for your answer and does not continue on its own.

data.name: Note_NoForce
data.value: Nothing is force-terminated without your separate confirmation.

data.name: Advice_Healthy_Text
data.value: Windows keeps recently used data in a cache (standby memory) and hands it to apps instantly when they need memory. That cache already counts as available, so no cleanup is needed.

data.name: Advice_Moderate_Text
data.value: If you need more memory, close apps you are not using — for example with Return to baseline. Clearing the cache does not increase available memory: cached memory is already available.

data.name: Advice_Low_Text
data.value: Apps are using most of the memory. Closing apps (Return to baseline) is what helps. Deep Memory Cleanup will not fix this, because it only drops cache that Windows would reuse anyway.

data.name: Advice_Unknown_Text
data.value: Windows did not report memory statistics.

data.name: Deep_CancelledByUser
data.value: Administrator permission was not granted. Nothing was changed.

data.name: Deep_PrivilegeMissing
data.value: The required system privilege is not available.

data.name: Deep_Failed
data.value: The cache could not be cleared (error {0}).

data.name: Deep_LaunchFailed
data.value: The elevated helper could not be started: {0}

data.name: Deep_UnknownExit
data.value: The elevated helper reported an unexpected result ({0}).

data.name: Cmp_ReclaimedByCleanup
data.value: Cache reclaimed by Deep Memory Cleanup

data.value: Part of WSL or Docker Desktop. SnapBack never closes these processes; stop WSL or Docker with their own action instead.

data.name: Profile_TooMany
data.value: You can have at most {0} profiles.

data.name: Impact_Explain_NothingSelected
data.value: No apps are selected, so nothing would change.

data.name: Impact_Explain_MostlyNotNew
data.value: Most memory in use is not caused by applications added after the baseline.

data.name: Impact_Explain_PlentyAvailable
data.value: Plenty of memory is available. Returning to the baseline mainly reduces clutter and background activity.

data.name: Impact_Explain_ShouldHelp
data.value: Memory is getting scarce and the new applications use a large part of it, so returning to the baseline should help noticeably.

data.name: Impact_Explain_Estimate
data.value: This is an estimate, not a promise: memory shared with other programs stays in use, apps may refuse to close, and Windows may keep part of the released memory as cache (which is still available).

data.name: Notify_Growth_Text
data.value: {0}: {1} → {2} in {3} h. This can be normal caching or a memory leak.

data.name: Env_Wsl_Warning
data.value: All WSL distributions and the WSL virtual machine will shut down (wsl --shutdown).

data.name: Env_Docker_Warning_Unknown

data.name: Env_Warning_Unsaved
